title: Elodie and the Trail
premise: Astrid Whitlock, a desert ranger who has spent three years chasing a thief named Elodie across the flats, is diverted when an archaeological expedition upriver goes silent. Following the dry riverbed to the wreck of a drowned courthouse, she discovers the expedition was murdered by the Meridian salvage fleet, which means to strip the wreck of its sealed records — records that could clear Elodie's name and convict the judge who framed her. Forced into an uneasy alliance with the thief she has hunted, Astrid races the fleet's six-tide deadline, choosing justice outside the law over the badge she no longer believes in. In the end, the records burn in Astrid's hands as she lets Elodie walk free, and Astrid walks back into the desert with no warrant, no thief, and, for the first time, no reason to keep moving.
about_author: Cyrus Oyelaran is a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping seasonal waterways before turning to fiction. He writes spare, sun-scorched adventure stories about people who outrun their pasts.

chapters.title: Six Tides of Nothing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Tracking Elodie across the salt flats, Astrid is ordered to abandon the chase when the Calloway expedition upriver misses three radio check-ins. She resents the diversion but obeys, following the dead riverbed toward the wreck. The beat is restlessness: a woman who only knows how to pursue, handed a pursuit she didn't choose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Courthouse
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She finds the expedition camp gutted and its leader dying, who tells her the salvage fleet killed them over the courthouse records. Catching Elodie raiding the same wreck, Astrid learns the thief's true name and the judge who erased her. The beat is reluctant alliance — hunter and hunted bound by a common enemy and a six-tide clock.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elodie leads Astrid through the flooded lower archive while the fleet's divers close in; Astrid discovers her own mentor signed the warrant that framed Elodie. They recover the record cylinder as the fleet detonates the wreck's supports. The beat is betrayal and resolve — Astrid's faith in the law collapses just as the escape route does.

chapters.title: Ash on the Flats
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cornered on a sinking causeway, Astrid burns the records in front of the fleet's captain, destroying the leverage and the proof alike, and covers Elodie's escape across the flats. She turns in her badge by radio and walks away alone. The beat is quiet release: justice done, unwitnessed, and the chase finally over.
